description: The ESA Space Weather Service Network portal contains space weather products, forecasts, alerts, archives and tools organised by user domain: spacecraft design and operation, human spaceflight, transionospheric radio links, space surveillance and tracking, non-space systems operation (power systems, pipelines, resource exploitation, auroral tourism) and general data. ESA runs it through its Space Safety Programme with a network of expert service centres; the power systems service, curated by the Geomagnetic Conditions centre, offers dB/dt forecasts, regional magnetograms, geomagnetically induced current (GIC) indices and peak GIC estimates for the UK, a local current index for Spain and modelled pipe-to-soil voltages. Coverage centres on Europe for ground effects and is global for solar wind and orbital products, from near-real-time to archive. The portal is accessible online; a dashboard of current conditions is open, while full access to forecasts, archives and tools needs free registration. Caveats: the portal states that all services are under review or construction, products come from many providers with differing terms, and pipe-to-soil voltages omit corrosion protection. It serves space weather hazard exposure, resilience and emergency response planning for power grids, pipelines, satellites and aviation; related records are SuperMAG, INTERMAGNET, the GFZ Kp index and the NOAA SWPC products.
